newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $10 lower Thursday on the heels of a weak performance in London overnight, dealers said.
"If London is going to continue going down, I guess we're going to to follow suit," one trader said.

LIFFE cocoa futures slumped early Thursday as operators focused on outright sales of July. At the midday break, July was down 13 stg at a a session low of 984 stg per tonne, while spot May slipped 14 stg to 954 stg.

Wednesday, New York cocoa futures sunk to fresh eight-week lows, pressured by continued speculative liquidation. July ended $14 lower at $1,400 a tonne after ranging from $1,410 to $1,392. Spot May fell the same to $1,394, while the back months closed $12 lower to $6 higher.

On the charts, traders saw nearby July support toward a trendline at $1,388-$1,386, with a solid downside target noted at $1,365. Resistance was seen near yesterday's close at $1,414, followed by $1,420.

On the fundamental side, International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) put the 1996/97 world cocoa deficit at 115,000 tonnes compared with its February forecast of a 225,000 tonne deficit and a 160,000-tonnes surplus last year.

ICCO said its reduced deficit projection was due to increased world output, due to upward revisions in African production. It increased its world 1996/97 cocoa production estimate by 93,000 tonnes, to 2.715 million tonnes.
ICCO raised its Ivory Coast crop forecast by 125,000 tonnes to 1.125 million tonnes. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
